page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 31 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 8 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the server allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU features a large 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance includes a bundled 137 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage, but does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of single-core strength and multi-core or memory bandwidth limitations. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression and text processing. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression fall into the weak category, reflecting the physical limitation of its 2-core configuration. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block reads are average, uncached large-block read bandwidth is poor, and the overall Passmark memory score is weak. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput are weak, though Redis SET operations maintain average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4-lssd provides a dense memory allocation and dedicated CPU resources with integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. However, the performance-per-resource tradeoff is highly specialized. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, such as single-threaded text processing, lightweight caching layers, and moderate-scale database operations. It is less suitable for high-throughput web serving, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or memory-bandwidth-bound applications.
